SELECT with ACCESS MODE.description: ACCESS MODE defines how records of the file are made available for processing your program. If ACCESS MODE is not specified Sequential (QSAM) is the default.

ACCEPT FROM.description: ACCEPT is typically used to extract the current date/time from z/OS. The other primary use case is ACCEPT from the JOB Step's SYSIN. Each line in SYSIN is tied to an individual ACCEPT statement. There are numerous options for date/time formatting.

ADDRESS OF.description: The ADDRESS OF special register references the address of a data item in the linkage section, the local-storage section, or the working-storage section.

ADD.description: ADD a TO b GIVING c

ADD CORRESPONDING.description: ADD CORRESPONDING is used to add the corresponding variables or fields in two identical group variables

ADD ON SIZE ERROR.description: ADD is an alternative to the COMPUTE statement for simple math operations. ON SIZE ERROR checks for truncation in the sum.

ADVANCING.description: The WRITE AFTER ADVANCING phrase in the PROCEDURE DIVISION gives the COBOL programmer control over report file processing and pagination. Note that OUTPUT-RECORD-FILE-STATUS-CODE must be defined in the file FD and declared as a two-byte PIC XX field in the WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. This variable automates the process of validating each I/O action and z/OS updates its value after each action.

ALPHABETIC.description: A COBOL "class test" used to determine whether the contents of a variable contains specific upper/lower case values. Used in conjunction with CMPR2/NOCMPR2 as compilation directives.

ALPHANUMERIC.description: A COBOL "class test" which is used to determine whether the contents of a variable only contain letters and numbers (no special characters).

IF x AND y.description: AND is used to connect two or more conditional expressions. When using AND - all expressions connected by AND must test true for the program to take that path.

AREA.description: The AREA/AREAS keywords force z/OS to use the same main storage area for performing internal file processing. The three instances are syntax checked, but have no effect on the program at run-time.

BEFORE ADVANCING.description: The WRITE BEFORE phrase in the PROCEDURE DIVISION gives the COBOL programmer control over file (most often report file) processing pagination. Note that OUTPUT-RECORD-FILE-STATUS-CODE must be defined in the file FD and declared as a two-byte (PIC XX) field in the WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

BINARY.description: Variables defined with BINARY (and synonyms COMP and COMP-4) are a two's complement data representation in the COBOL language. This example provides two bytes of values in Base 16.

BIT TO CHAR.description: Calls BIT-TO-CHAR to obtain a string that corresponds to the bit pattern stored in the PIC X field.

BLANK WHEN ZERO.description: BLANK WHEN ZERO specifies that an elementary field contains spaces when its value is zero.

BLOCK.description: The BLOCK CONTAINS clause in the FD entry in the DATA DIVISION dictates the size of the physical (I/O) records. If you specify BLOCK CONTAINS 0, z/OS chooses the optimal "blocking factor" for most efficient file I/O - taking into account channels and DASD along with the file specifics.

BOOLEAN.prefix: JSON GENERATE FROM then CONVERT TO BOOLEAN
BOOLEAN.description: BOOLEAN as a reserved word is typically used to convert COBOL data to non-JSON data format.

BOTTOM.description: Part of the DATA DIVISION file FD, LINAGE clause, LINES AT BOTTOM tells COBOL to setup a bottom margin (blank lines at the bottom of every logical page).

INDEXED BY.description: Defines an internal COBOL index for an internal COBOL table.

SET x UP BY.description: Adds +1 an internal COBOL table's index - assuming INDEXED BY.

STRING x DELIMITED BY y.description: BY in the STRING (and UNSTRING) statements defines the transfer operation specifics: INTO VAR-3.

CALL.description: The CALL statement transfers control from one compiled program to another. Note that the BY and RETURNING clauses are optional. For more on CALL:

CANCEL.description: The CANCEL statement terminates the subprogram. This ensures that data in the subprogram reverts to its initial state the next time the subprogram is called. Also when a CANCEL statement is executed all called programs contained within the program referenced in the CANCEL statement are canceled.

CHARACTERS.description: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION / CONFIGURATION SECTION - SYMBOLIC CHARACTER

CODE SET.description: DATA DIVISION / FILE SECTION - CODE-SET is used in the COBOL DATA DIVISION, FILE SECTION, FD entry.

COLLATING.description: Part of the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. Note that the default option is EBCDIC

COMP.description: BINARY, and its synonyms COMP and COMP-4, are used next to numeric fields in the DATA DIVISION to specify that the data is represented in two's complement hex (EBCDIC) format.

COMP-1.description: A four-byte single-precision floating-point number declared in the DATA DIVISION.

COMP-2.description: A four-byte double-precision floating-point number declared in the DATA DIVISION.

COMP-3.description: Internally-packed (efficient) number declared in the DATA DIVISION.

COMP-4.description: BINARY, and its synonyms COMP and COMP-4, are used next to numeric fields in the DATA DIVISION to specify that the data is represented in two's complement hex (EBCDIC) format.

COMP-5.description: Typically used to communicate data between Java/C/C++/Python/etc. and COBOL. When numeric data is moved into a COMP-5 item, truncation occurs at the binary field size rather than at the COBOL picture clause declaration.

body: NOT ON SIZE ERROR GO TO ${6:PROGRAM-FINAL-ACTION}
COMPUTE.description: COMPUTE provides an algebraic-style keyword for the specification of complex arithmetic expressions: + (add), - (subtract), * (multiply), / (divide), ** (power of) and any intrinsic functions that return numeric results. ON SIZE ERROR allows you to trap situations such as divide by zero and result overflow.

body: NOT ON SIZE ERROR GO TO ${7:PROGRAM-FINAL-ACTION}
COMPUTE (CICS).description: COMPUTE provides an algebraic-style keyword for the specification of complex arithmetic expressions: + (add), - (subtract), * (multiply), / (divide), ** (power of) and any intrinsic functions that return numeric results. ON SIZE ERROR allows you to trap situations such as divide by zero and result overflow.

CONFIGURATION.description: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION - The CONFIGURATION SECTION describes the z/OS environment on which the program is compiled and executed. It is an optional section for programs, functions, prototypes, and classes.

CONTAINS.description: A fixed-block file. Note that BLOCK CONTAINS 0 leaves the blocking-optimization up to z/OS - and is the preferred way to specify most QSAM file FDs.

CONTENT-OF.description: The CONTENT-OF intrinsic function produces a temporary copy of the input argument.

CONTINUE.description: The CONTINUE statement is a no-op. It indicates that no instruction is present and that execution falls to the next sequential instruction.

CONTROL.description: *CONTROL is a compiler option which allows the user to limit (or not limit) the MAP output of a program compile.

CONVERTING.description: CONVERTING is a parameter of the INSPECT keyword - used to replace character values.

COPY.description: COPY is used to insert source code stored in a PDS or SCM into a COBOL program when it is compiled. Note that the JCL or Source Management System (Endevor, etc.) must be available and specified correctly during compilation.

COUNT.description: Part of the UNSTRING statement, the COUNT phrase specifies the field where the count of examined character positions is held.

CRT.description: Part of the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph/CONFIGURATION SECTION in the ENVIRONMENT DIVISION. CRT STATUS returns data regarding the status of a screen-based COBOL ACCEPT statement when an ON EXCEPTION statement is included in the ACCEPT statement.

body: CURRENCY SIGN IS "${1:\$USD}" WITH PICTURE SYMBOL "${2:\$}".
CURRENCY.description: The CURRENCY SIGN clause is defined in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph in the CONFIGURATION SECTION of the ENVIRONMENT DIVISION. You can declare multiple currency signs for multiple currencies.

CURSOR.description: CURSOR IS is the name of a numeric data item described in the WORKING-STORAGE SECTION, which contains a value for placement of the cursor on a CRT. CURSOR IS is defined in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph.

AT DATE.description: AT DATE is used with the IBM COBOL Debugger. It gives the Debugger control for each date processing statement within the specified block. In the above example: Each time a date processing statement is encountered in the compile unit; 1. Display the location of the statement 2. List a specific variable, and 3. Resume running the program.

DATE COMPILED YYYY/MM/DD.description: DATE-COMPILED is an optional statement in the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION that describes the specific date of program compilation.

DATE COMPILED MM/DD/YYYY.description: DATE-COMPILED is an optional statement in the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION that describes the specific date of program compilation.

DATE WRITTEN YYYY/MM/DD.description: DATE-WRITTEN is an optional statement in the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION that describes the specific date of program compilation.

DATE WRITTEN MM/DD/YYYY.description: DATE-WRITTEN is an optional statement in the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION that describes the specific date of program compilation.

DAY.description: This is an example of utilizing a Julian Date receiving field (PIC 9(5) variable - YY NNN) - from z/OS.

DAY OF WEEK.description: This is an example of utilizing a one-byte (ie. PIC 9(1)) receiving variable - (1-7) from z/OS. Note that 1 = Monday, 2 = Tuesday, 3 = Wednesday, etc.

DBCS.description: A class-condition, allowing you to test whether the data in a field is in valid DBCS format.

DEBUG-ITEM (Simplified).description: The DEBUG-ITEM special register provides information for a debugging declarative procedure about the conditions that cause debugging section execution.

body: 02 FILLER PICTURE IS X VALUE SPACE.
02 FILLER PICTURE IS X VALUE SPACE.
02 DEBUG-SUB-1 PICTURE IS S9999 SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE CHARACTER.
02 FILLER PICTURE IS X VALUE SPACE.
02 DEBUG-SUB-2 PICTURE IS S9999 SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE CHARACTER.
02 FILLER PICTURE IS X VALUE SPACE.
02 DEBUG-SUB-3 PICTURE IS S9999 SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE CHARACTER.
02 FILLER PICTURE IS X VALUE SPACE.
DEBUG-ITEM (Implicit Description).description: The DEBUG-ITEM special register provides information for a debugging declarative procedure about the conditions that cause debugging section execution. This is the implicit description of the DEBUG-ITEM special register.

DECIMAL-POINT.description: Part of the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA clause exchanges the functions of the period and the comma in PIC character-strings and in numeric literals.

DECLARATIVES 1.description: Declaratives provide one or more special-purpose sections that are executed when an exception occurs.

DECLARATIVES 2.description: Declaratives provide one or more special-purpose sections that are executed when an exception occurs.

INITIALIZE DEFAULT.description: PROCEDURE DIVISION - The INITIALIZE statement sets selected categories of data fields to predetermined values. The INITIALIZE statement is functionally equivalent to one or more MOVE statements.

DELETE.description: Deletes a record from a file.

DEPENDING.description: OCCURS DEPENDING ON (ODO) specifies variable-length internal COBOL tables.

DESCENDING.description: Using the binary (efficient) table SEARCH ALL option, DESCENDING declares that the internal COBOL table rows are sorted in descending order based upon values in a specified field within the table.

DISPLAY.description: Show the value of a COBOL variable on a screen or write it to an output file by using a DISPLAY statement.

DISPLAY-1.description: The DISPLAY-1 phrase defines an item as DBCS. The data item is stored in character form, with each character occupying 2 bytes of storage.

DIVIDE.description: In this example, NUMVAR-1 is divided by NUMVAR-2 and the result is stored in NUMVAR-3, rounded to the nearest whole number. If NUMVAR-1 = 0 or the quotient is larger than the pic-clause of NUMVAR-3, the ON SIZE ERROR is executed. That would typically be a GO TO statement referencing a paragraph written to handle errors such as this.

body: DIVIDE INTO GIVING REMAINDER=DIVIDE ${1:id} INTO ${2:id} GIVING ${3:id} REMAINDER ${4:id4}

ALTERNATE RECORD with DUPLICATES.description: DUPLICATES allows an indexed VSAM file to be defined with duplicate values declared in a defined variable within the record in the FD.

SORT with DUPLICATES.description: IN ORDER forces the z/OS SORT utility to retain the original order of the input file, if duplicate key-field values are found. Note that IN ORDER is an optional clause of WITH DUPLICATES.

DYNAMIC.description: Allows the specific READ/WRITE statement to determine the access mode. Records can be processed sequentially or randomly or both.

EGCS.description: Initializes a variable while replacing the EGCS (Extended Graphic Character Set) information by a value or variable.

IF-ELSE.description: IF ... ELSE codes a choice between two COBOL processing actions.

ENTRY.description: The ENTRY statement establishes an alternate entry point into a COBOL called subprogram.

body: ENTRY ${1:literal} USING${2| , BY REFERENCE , BY VALUE |}${3:LINKAGE-DATA-ITEM}.
ENTRY USING.description: The ENTRY statement establishes an alternate entry point into a COBOL called subprogram.

EOP.description: EOP is a synonym for END-OF-PAGE.

ERROR #1.description: NUMVAR-1 is divided into NUMVAR-2. If NUMVAR-1 = 0 or if the quotient is larger than NUMVAR-3 the ON SIZE ERROR statement is executed. If ON SIZE ERROR is not coded, the program abends.

ERROR #2.description: The like-named variables in the COBOL group field GROUP-FIELDS-1 are moved to GROUP-FIELDS-2. If there are any variables in GROUP-FIELDS-1 that are larger than the same named variable in GROUP-FIELDS-2 the ON SIZE ERROR statement is executed. If ON SIZE ERROR is not coded, the program abends.

ERROR #3.description: The EXCEPTION/ERROR declarative specifies procedures for input/output exception or error handling that are to be executed in addition to the standard z/OS procedures.

EVERY (XML).description: Part of the COBOL XML statement.

EXCEPTION #2.description: An EXCEPTION condition occurs when the XML document cannot be generated.

EXCEPTION #3.description: An EXCEPTION condition occurs when there is a problem closing a QSAM, VSAM or Line Sequential.

EXIT.description: EXIT statements close the PERFORM CHAIN (internal COBOL iterative control structure). Control is returned to the NSI (Next Sequential Instruction) following the PERFORM statement.

EXIT PROGRAM.description: EXIT PROGRAM transfers control outside the COBOL program.

EXIT PROGRAM RETURNING.description: EXIT PROGRAM transfers control outside the COBOL program.

EXIT METHOD.description: EXIT METHOD transfers control outside the Object COBOL program.

ARITH EXTEND.description: A compiler directive that provides extended-precision function results that can accurately represent the value of the argument being returned.

EXTERNAL.description: The EXTERNAL clause specifies that the main storage associated with a data item is associated with the run unit rather than with any particular program.

EVALUATE.description: Use EVALUATE instead of a series of nested IF statements to test multiple conditions and specify distinct actions for each.

EVALUATE FALSE.description: Use EVALUATE instead of a series of nested IF statements to test multiple conditions and specify distinct actions for each.

FD (QSAM).description: DATA DIVISION - The FD describes files referred to in the PRODUCTION DIVISION's I/O statements.

FD (VSAM).description: DATA DIVISION - The VSAM FD describes files referred to in the PROCEDURE DIVISION's I/O statements.

FILE SECTION.description: DATA DIVISION - The FILE SECTION is where you define specifics of each input/output file.

FILE STATUS.description: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION - FILE STATUS defines a two-byte (PIC XX) field that recieves a code from z/OS based on the disposition of the I/O operation.

MULTIPLE FILE TAPE.description: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION / INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION / FILE-CONTROL - The MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause specifies that 2 or mote data files, separated by commas, share the same physical volume serial of tape.

FILE CONTROL.description: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION / INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION / FILE-CONTROL - The FILE-CONTROL paragraph associates every file in your COBOL program with an external data set. It optionally defines file organization, access mode, etc.

FILLER.description: A placeholder variable that is not explicitly referred to in a program. FILLER is used to line up variable names with byte-offsets in the physical data record.

FIRST #2.description: REPLACING FIRST changes the first (leftmost) occurrence of the inspected field (VAR-1 in this example).

FOOTING.description: Part of the FD LINAGE (logical page size) clause - available for QSAM and LINE-SEQUENTIAL files only. WITH FOOTING specifies a line number in an output file or printer.

FOR CHARACTERS AFTER.description: Counts the number of characters after the first occurrence of a specified string. Part of the TALLYING keyword in the INSPECT statement.

USE FOR DEBUGGING.description: PRODECURE DIVISION - Specifies debugging to begin on (specified) routine.

CLOSE x FOR REMOVAL.description: This phrase applies only to TAPE/REEL data sets and is treated as a comment.

body: PERFORM ${1:B-100PARAGRAPH} VARYING ${2:IDX-1} FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL ${2:IDX-1} > TABLE-MAX-ROWS
FROM #1.description: The "FROM" in a PERFORM VARYING clause sets the initial value and the incremental/iterative value(s) for a table subscript or index.

FROM #2.description: The FROM phrase is equivalent to: MOVE REC-1 to OUTPUT-REC WRITE OUTPUT-REC.

FROM #3.description: This statement values the receiving-field with one of the system date registers.

FUNCTION BIT-TO-CHAR.description: FUNCTION TO CONVERT BITS TO CHARACTER

FUNCTION CHAR.description: FUNCTION CHARACTER IN THE ORDINAL POSITION SPECIFIED BY INTEGER, FROM THE CURRENT ALPHANUMERIC COLLATING SEQUENCE

FUNCTION CURRENCY-SYMBOL.description: FUNCTION CURRENCY-SYMBOL CHARACTER CURRENTLY IN EFFECT FOR THE LOCALE UNDER WHICH THE PROGRAM IS RUNNING

FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE.description: FUNCTION CURRENT DATE AND TIME AS 21-CHARACTER VALUE

FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER.description: FUNCTION TO CONVERT THE INTEGER DATE TO STANDARD DATE FORMAT

FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER.description: FUNCTION TO CONVERT THE INTEGER DATE TO NUMBER OF DAYS IN THE GREGORIAN CALENDAR

FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD.description: FUNCTION TO CONVERT A DATE WITH A 2 DIGIT YEAR TO A 4 DIGIT YEAR

FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF.description: FUNCTION TO CONVERT AN ALPHANUMERIC STRING USING A CODEPAGE

FUNCTION EXP.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN E RAISED TO THE POWER OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION ACOS.description: FUNCTION TRIGONOMETRIC ARC-COSINE, OR INVERSE COSINE, OF COSINE

FUNCTION ASIN.description: FUNCTION TRIGONOMETRIC ARC-SINE, OR INVERSE SINE, OF SINE

FUNCTION ATAN.description: FUNCTION TRIGONOMETRIC ARC-TANGENT, OR INVERSE TANGENT, OF TANGENT

FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER.description: FUNCTION BOOLEAN ITEM OF USAGE BIT REPRESENTING THE BINARY VALUE OF INTEGER; WITH THE GIVEN LENGTH

FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD.description: FUNCTION TO CONVERT A DATE WITH A 2 DIGIT YEAR TO A 4 DIGIT YEAR

FUNCTION EXP10.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN 10 RAISED TO THE POWER OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION FACTORIAL.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN THE FACTORIAL OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION HEX-OF.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN HEXADECIMAL REPRESENTATION OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION HEX-TO-CHAR.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN A CHARACTER STRING THAT IS A HEXADECIMAL REPRESENTATION OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION INTEGER.description: GREATEST INTEGER VALUE THAT IS LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO NUMBER

FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE.description: CONVERTS YYYYMMDD TO AN INTERNAL INTEGER-DATE

FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY.description: CONVERTS YYYYMMDD TO AN INTERNAL INTEGER-DAY

FUNCTION INTEGER-PART.description: PORTION OF NUMBER THAT OCCURS TO THE LEFT OF THE DECIMAL POINT

FUNCTION LENGTH.description: RETURNS THE LENGTH (IN CHARACTER POSITIONS) OF THE SPECIFIED ITEM

FUNCTION LOG.description: FORMAT BASE E LOGARITHM OF NUMBER

FUNCTION LOWERCASE.description: CHARACTER STRING THAT CONTAINS STRING WITH ANY UPPERCASE LETTERS REPLACED BY THEIR CORRESPONDING LOWERCASE LETTERS

FUNCTION MAX.description: ALPHANUMERIC/INDEX/INTEGER/NATIONAL/NUMERIC MAXIMUM VALUE FROM THE SPECIFIED LIST OF NUMBERS

FUNCTION MEAN.description: STATISTICAL MEAN VALUE OF THE SPECIFIED LIST OF NUMBERS

FUNCTION MEDIAN.description: STATISTICAL MEDIAN VALUE OF THE SPECIFIED LIST OF NUMBERS

FUNCTION MIDRANGE.description: STATISTICAL MIDRANGE VALUE OF THE SPECIFIED LIST OF NUMBERS

FUNCTION MIN.description: STATISTICAL MIN VALUE OF THE SPECIFIED LIST OF NUMBERS

FUNCTION MOD.description: REMAINDER FROM THE DIVISION OF VALUE BY MODULUS

FUNCTION NATIONAL-OF.description: CONVERT ALPHANUMERIC-STRING TO THE NATIONAL CODED CHARACTER SET REPRESENTATION

FUNCTION NUMVAL-C.description: CORRESPONDING NUMERIC VALUE FOR STRING, CASE-SENSITIVE IF ANYCASE NOT GIVEN

FUNCTION ORD.description: ORDINAL POSITION IN THE PROGRAM CHARACTER SET CORRESPONDING TO CHAR

FUNCTION ORD-MAX.description: MAX. ORDINAL POSITION IN THE PROGRAM CHARACTER SET CORRESPONDING TO LIST OF CHARS

FUNCTION ORD-MIN.description: MIN. ORDINAL POSITION IN THE PROGRAM CHARACTER SET CORRESPONDING TO LIST OF CHARS

FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE.description: APPROXIMATION OF THE PRESENT VALUE OF A SERIES OF FUTURE PERIOD-END AMOUNT

FUNCTION RANDOM.description: PSEUDO-RANDOM NUMBER 0> <1 FROM A RECTANGULAR DISTRIBUTION WITH OPTIONAL SEED

FUNCTION RANGE.description: VALUE OF THE MAXIMUM ARGUMENT MINUS THE VALUE OF THE MINIMUM ARGUMENT

FUNCTION REM.description: REMAINDER OF NUMBER DIVIDED BY DIVISOR

FUNCTION REVERSE.description: REVERSE REPRESENTATION WITH SAME LENGTH OF STRING

FUNCTION SIN.description: TRIGONOMETRIC SINE OF THE SPECIFIED ANGLE

FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN THE STANDARD DEVIATION OF ITS ARGUMENTS

FUNCTION SQRT.description: APPROXIMATION OF THE SQUARE ROOT OF NUMBER

FUNCTION SUM.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN THE SUM OF ITS ARGUMENTS

FUNCTION TAN.description: TRIGONOMETRIC TANGENT OF THE SPECIFIED ANGLE

FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL.description: FUNCTION TO VERIFY THE CONTENTS OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F.description: FUNCTION TO VERIFY THE CONTENTS OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION TRIM.description: FUNCTION TO TRIM LEADING AND OR TRAILING SPACES OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION ULENGTH.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN THE NUMBER OF UTF8 OR UTF16 CHARACTERS OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION UPOS.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN AN INTEGER VALUE EQUAL TO THE POSITION OF THE NTH ITEM IN THE PASSED UTF8 OR UTF16 ARGUMENT

FUNCTION UPPER-CASE.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN THE ARGUMENT IN UPPER CASE

FUNCTION USUBSTR.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN SUBSTRING OF THE CHARACTER DATA PASSED THAT CONTAINS UTF8 OR UTF16 DATA

FUNCTION USUPPLEMENTARY.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN AN INTEGER VALUE EQUATING TO THE INDEX OF THE FIRST UNICODE CHARACTER OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION UVALID.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN AN INTEGER VALUE EQUATING TO THE INDEX OF THE FIRST INVALID UNICODE CHARACTER OF THE ARGUMENT

FUNCTION UWIDTH.description: FUNCTION TO RETURN AN INTEGER VALUE EQUAL TO THE WIDTH IN BYTES OF THE NTH ITEM IN THE PASSED UTF8 OR UTF16 ARGUMENT

FUNCTION VARIANCE.description: STATISTICAL VARIANCE OF THE SPECIFIED LIST OF NUMBER ARGUMENT

FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY.description: CONVERT YY TO YYYY WITH OPTIONAL YY-CUTOFF TO DELINEATE CENTURIES

FUNCTION-POINTER.description: A FUNCTION-POINTER is a 4-byte elementary item which can contain the address of a procedure (typically a program) entry point.

JSON GENERATE.description: Manipulate COBOL data items as JSON text by using the JSON GENERATE statement.

XML GENERATE.description: Use an XML GENERATE statement to transform COBOL data to XML.

GOBACK.description: Ends program and returns control to the application module that invoked the program. If this is a standalone batch program, GOBACK returns control to z/OS.

GREATER.description: GREATER is a general comparison operator - treated like the algebraic ">" operator.

GROUP-USAGE.description: A group item that is described with an explicit or implicit GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL clause is a national group item. Note that NATIONAL data items are represented as UTF-16 characters.

HIGH-VALUES.description: HIGH-VALUE equates to binary (Hex) FF - the highest EBCDIC collating sequence value.

I-O.description: Use the input-output file mode to rewrite QSAM and VSAM file records in place.

ID DIVISION.description: The IDENTIFICATION DIVISION contains the PROGRAM-ID, AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATE-WRITTEN, and SECURITY paragraphs.

INSPECT CONVERTING.description: INSPECT is a string parsing verb for alphanumeric fields.

INSPECT REPLACING.description: INSPECT is a string parsing verb for alphanumeric fields.

IN #1.description: COUNT IN references an integer field that contains the number of characters placed in the current receiving field.

IN #2.description: DELIMITER IN references a PIC X field that contains the DELIMITER character placed in the UNSTRING field.

IN #3.description: TALLYING IN references a numeric field that contains a total of the number of fields that are acted on during the UNSTRING.

INDEX.description: USAGE IS INDEX creates an index data item, which can used as an index variable into any COBOL internal table (OCCURS clause).

OCCURS x INDEXED BY.description: INDEXED BY defines an internal COBOL index data item and associates it with a given COBOL table.

ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED.description: IS INDEXED defines a file entry as a VSAM KSDS (Indexed) Data Set in the ENVIRONMENT DIVISION'S SELECT/ASSIGN paragraph.

ACCESS MODE IS INPUT.description: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION / INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION / FILE-CONTROL - File I/O mode that denotes if input is to be read from a file.

INITIALIZE.description: Use INITIALIZE instead of multiple MOVE statements to set a Group data structure to its initial values.

INPUT-OUTPUT.description: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION - The INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION of the ENVIRONMENT DIVISION contains FILE-CONTROL and I-O-CONTROL paragraphs. The contents of the INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION depend on specific file organization and access methods.

READ INTO.description: READ INTO reads then copies records from FD buffers into WORKING-STORAGE data items.

RETURN INTO.description: RETURN INTO accesses a sorted file record and copies it into a WORKING-STORAGE data item.

INSTALLATION.description: IDENTIFICATION DIVISION - Use the optional INSTALLATION clause to uniquely name the z/OS system.

INVALID KEY (VSAM).description: INVALID KEY can be used in VSAM KSDS and RRDS files for: READ, START, WRITE, REWRITE, and DELETE statements. The INVALID KEY imperative statement is given control if an I/O error occurs due to a defective VSAM file index key.

INVALID KEY (QSAM).description: For QSAM files, the INVALID KEY phrase can be used in WRITE requests. It is executed if you attempt to write to a I/O disk (VOL=SER) that is full.

ACCESS IS.description: File specifics with IS. (IS is optional)

USAGE IS.description: Variable declarations with IS. (IS is optional)

JNIENVPTR.description: JNIENVPTR is a COBOL special register that references the JNI pointer as declared in the JNI.cpy copybook. It is used when interfacing Java with COBOL. Special registers are reserved words that name storage areas generated by the compiler.

body: 01 JSON-CODE PIC S9(9) USAGE BINARY VALUE 0.
JSON-CODE.description: JSON-CODE is a special register used to indicate that a JSON GENERATE or JSON PARSE statement executed successfully or that an exception occurred.

body: 01 JSON-STATUS PIC S9(9) USAGE BINARY VALUE 0.
JSON-STATUS.description: JSON-STATUS is a special register used to indicate that a JSON GENERATE or JSON PARSE statement executed successfully or that an exception occurred.

JUST.description: The JUST/JUSTIFIED clause overrides standard positioning rules for receiving items of category alphabetic, alphanumeric, DBCS, or national.

KANJI.description: One of several class conditional statements. Checks whether a variable entirely contains KANJI characters.

ASCENDING KEY #1.description: ASCENDING KEY in a table OCCURS clause allows you to use a COBOL SEARCH ALL construct.

ASCENDING KEY #2.description: ASCENDING KEY in a table OCCURS clause allows you to use a COBOL SEARCH ALL construct.

RECORD KEY.description: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION / FILE-CONTROL - RECORD KEY declares a field that you define in the FILE SECTION to be used to search the indexed/VSAM data. The same technique can be used for SORT Files.

LABEL RECORDS.description: DATA DIVISION / FILE SECTION - For QSAM files, LABEL RECORDS declares the presence or absence of labels used to identify DASD volumes - for uncataloged files. For VSAM files LABEL RECORDS is syntax checked but ignored.

LEADING.description: SIGN LEADING/TRAILING declares the position of the operational sign for a numeric variable.

LEFT.description: LEFT Specifies that an elementary COBOL variable is to be positioned in main storage so that byte one begins at the left word boundary. Note that this is an efficiency coding specification.

LENGTH.description: Find and use the LENGTH of COBOL variables and group structures.

LESS.description: LESS is a general comparison operator - treated like the algebraic "<" operator.

LINEAGE.description: DATA DIVISION - The LINEAGE clause of a FD entry controls the size and number of lines of a printed page.

WRITE LINE.description: Use LINE to control the number of blank lines output for a report file.

LINE SEQUENTIAL.description: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION - LINE-SEQUENTIAL defines an input/output file as a line-sequential file - typically Unix or PC.

LOCAL-STORAGE.description: LOCAL-STORAGE defines variables that are allocated and freed on a per-program invocation basis. Every program invocation reallocates the LOCAL-STORAGE variables and resets variable values to their declared initial values.

CLOSE x WITH LOCK.description: CLOSE WITH LOCK ensures that the file cannot be opened again while the program is executing.

body: READ ${1:IN-FILE} AT END MOVE LOW-VALUES TO ${2:INPUT-REC}.
READ LOW-VALUE.description: For Alphanumeric fields - LOW-VALUE/LOW-VALUES equates to binary (Hex) 00 - the lowest EBCDIC collating sequence value.

MOVE LOW-VALUE.description: For Alphanumeric fields - LOW-VALUE/LOW-VALUES equates to binary (Hex) 00 - the lowest EBCDIC collating sequence value.

IF LOW-VALUE.description: For Alphanumeric fields - LOW-VALUE/LOW-VALUES equates to binary (Hex) 00 - the lowest EBCDIC collating sequence value.

MERGE ASCENDING.description: The Merge statement fuses two or more identially sorted files on one or more variable-keys and makes the merged records available to an OUTPUT PROCEDURE or output file.

ACCESS MODE.description: ACCESS MODE defines how records are made available for processing. If ACCESS MODE is not defined, the default is SEQUENTIAL.

RECORDING MODE.description: FILE SECTION - RECORDING MODE specifies the physical format of records in a QSAM file: F (fixed), V (variable), U (fixed or variable), S (spanned)

DEBUGGING MODE.description: WITH DEBUGGING MODE activates a compile-switch for debugging lines in the program.

MORE-LABELS.description: GO TO MORE-LABELS statement is specified only in a COBOL LABEL DECLARATIVE statement.

MOVE CORRESPONDING.description: After the above MOVE CORRESPONDING statement, all values in like-named-variables will be copied from GROUP-1 to GROUP-2.

MOVE.description: MOVE copies data from one variable to one or more other variables. Note that storage data and Figurative Constants (SPACES, HIGH-VALUES, LOW-VALUES, etc.) can be moved into variables.

MULTIPLY a BY b GIVING c.description: MULTIPLY a BY b GIVING c

MULTIPLY a BY b GIVING c ON SIZE ERROR.description: If ON SIZE ERROR is specified and a size error condition occurs (typically truncation in the product) the error result is not placed in the product and the imperative statement in the ON SIZE ERROR phrase is executed.

NATIONAL-EDITED #1.description: WORKING-STORAGE SECTION - NATIONAL/NATIONAL-EDITED data items are variables whose content is represented in UTF-16 (often referred to as Unicode).

NATIONAL-EDITED #2.description: PROCEDURE DIVISION - NATIONAL/NATIONAL-EDITED data (or data items within a group field) are replaced by the same-named variables in VAR-2 in the given example.

NATIVE.description: NATIVE is syntax checked, but has no effect on program execution.

NEXT SENTENCE.description: NEXT SENTENCE transfers control to the next sequential instruction following the closest period (separator).

NEXT RECORD.description: NEXT RECORD is a phrase that reads the next record from an input file. NEXT is optional for QSAM files, but you must specify NEXT RECORD to retrieve records sequentially from a VSAM file.

body: DISPLAY "${1:ERROR IN OPENING FILE}" WITH NO ADVANCING.
NO ADVANCING.description: When used, the positioning of the output device will not be changed.

NO REWIND.description: NO REWIND applies only to LINE-SEQUENTIAL and QSAM tape files.  Specifically, with NO REWIND, OPEN filename must be positioned at its beginning record.

IF var NOT x.description: NOT is a true/false test - testing true if the comparison fails.

body: NOT ON SIZE ERROR ${4:MOVE ZEROS TO VAR-4}
NOT ON SIZE ERROR.description: NOT is a true/false test - testing true if the comparison fails. In the snippet, if there is no numeric exception in the subtract, zeros are moved to VAR-4.

NULL.description: NULL which has the value of zero, is a data type used with datatypes of: POINTER, PROCEDURE-POINTER, FUNCTION-POINTER, OBJECT REFERENCE, or the ADDRESS OF a special register.

NUMERIC.description: IF NUMERIC is a conditional class test which can be applied to variable types: DISPLAY, NATIONAL, COMPUTATIONAL-3, or PACKED-DECIMAL.

body: INITIALIZE ${1:VAR1} REPLACING NUMERIC-EDITED DATA BY ${2:literal or variable}
NUMERIC-EDITED.description: NUMERIC-EDITED => Numeric data items with insertion characters.

OBJECT-COMPUTER.description: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION - The OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph details the mainframe for which the compiled object program is run on.

OBJECT-REFERENCE.description: An OBJECT-REFERENCE data item is a 4 or 8 byte (depending on your z/OS system) that references valid objects.

OCCURS.description: OCCURS is used to code a table by defining a number (N) of repeated subordinate rows.

OCCURS DEPENDING ON.description: OCCURS DEPENDING ON is used to code a table where you do not know how many rows are in the table.

MOVE x OF y TO.description: OF (qualification) allows you to uniquely specify a variable by referencing higher-level variable-names in a struction.

SET ADDRESS OF.description: ADDRESS OF is a COBOL special register that can be used to reference the address of a data item in the LINKAGE SECTION, LOCAL-STORAGE SECTION, or WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

INLINE OFF.description: This COBOL directive OFF prevents the compiler from inlining procedures referenced by PERFORM statements.

RECORDS ARE OMITTED.description: Used for Tape files without z/OS data set LABELS.

body: JSON PARSE ${1:VAR-1} INTO ${2:VAR-2} NAME IS OMITTED.
NAME IS OMITTED.description: Can use the NAME IS OMITTED phrase to parse an anonymous JSON array in addition to an anonymous JSON object.

DEPENDING ON.description: ON is used as part of a dynamic table declaration.

SET ptr ON.description: ON is used to set a pointer or 88-conditional to True.

ON SIZE ERROR.description: ON is used to code: ON SIZE ERROR, ON OVERFLOW and ON EXCEPTION error and exception trapping phrases.

body: OPEN INPUT ${1:fileName}${2|., REVERSED., WITH NO REWIND.|}
OPEN INPUT.description: OPEN INPUT initiates the process of reading files. Note that REVERSED and WITH NO REWIND are optional clauses.

OPEN OUTPUT.description: OPEN OUTPUT initiates the process of writing files. Note that NO REWIND is optional.

OPTIONAL.description: If SELECT OPTIONAL is specified in the file-control entry for this file, and the file is not available at runtime, execution of the first READ statement causes an at-end condition rather than an ABEND. This applies to QSAM and VSAM files opened for INPUT, I-O, or EXTEND.

If x OR y.description: A logical comparison operator. The truth value of OR is true when either or both conditions are met.

WHEN x OR y.description: A logical comparison operator that is part of an EVALUATE statement. The truth value of OR is true when either or both conditions are met.

DUPLICATES IN ORDER.description: If duplicate records are found, by coding DUPLICATES IN ORDER z/OS will maintain the physical order. Without this phrase, the sorting of duplicate records is undefined.

ORGANIZATION (QSAM).description: QSAM file accessed sequentially (one record after the next).

body: ACCESS MODE IS ${4|SEQUENTIAL,RANDOM,DYNAMIC|} RECORD KEY IS ${5:key1}.
ORGANIZATION (VSAM).description: VSAM file ORGANIZATION clause for a VSAM file accessed through the file's index (key1).

OTHER.description: In an EVALUATE statement if no WHEN phrase is selected and WHEN OTHER is specified, execution continues with the OTHER statement.

OUTPUT PROCEDURE.description: PROCEDURE DIVISION - In a SORT or MERGE statement OUTPUT PROCEDURE specifies the name of a COBOL SECTION or paragraph that selects and/or modifies output records from the SORT/MERGE operation.

ON OVERFLOW GO TO (Unstring Statement).description: ON OVERFLOW with UNSTRING allows you to trap text-parsing errors during runtime. After ON OVERFLOW you can code any imperative statement.

body: STRING ${1:PATIENT-NO SPACE PATIENT-NAME INV-NO SPACE DATE-PROCESS SPACE}
ON OVERFLOW GO TO (String Statement).description: ON OVERFLOW with STRING allows you to trap text-parsing errors during runtime. After ON OVERFLOW you can code any imperative statement.

ON OVERFLOW GO TO (Call Statement).description: ON OVERFLOW with CALL statements allows you to trap runtime called program name errors. Without ON OVERFLOW the program will ABEND. After ON OVERFLOW you can code any imperative statement.

PACKED-DECIMAL.description: PACKED-DECIMAL variables (internally) are stored with two digits for each character position, except for the trailing character position, which is occupied by the low-order digit and the variable's sign. PACKED-DECIMAL is identical to COMP-3/COMPUTATIONAL-3.

PADDING CHARACTER IS.description: PADDING CHARACTER specifies a character, or variable defined in WORKING-STORAGE, to be used for record-blocking-factor padding on sequential files. (That is, filling out a BLOCK of records. BLOCK is the unit of file I/O between DFSMS and your program's DATA DIVISION.)

PERFORM TIMES.description: PERFORM TIMES PROCEDURE NAME X TIMES

PERFORM THRU.description: PERFORM THRU transfers control to one or more paragraphs or SECTIONS and returns control to the next sequential executable statement after the THRU paragraph or SECTION finishes.

PICTURE.description: The reserved word PICTURE or PIC describes a data variable to the COBOL compiler (and program).

POINTER.description: POINTER defines a variable as a 4 or 8 byte field. This is dependent on the LP(nn) Compiler directive, which contains the address of a variable, instead of its contents.

POINTER-32.description: POINTER-32 defines a variable as a 4 byte field. This is independent of the LP(nn) Compiler directive, which contains the address of a variable, instead of its contents.

POSITIVE.description: POSITIVE is a "sign condition" used to determine whether the algebraic value of a numeric variable is greater than zero.

PROCEDURE DIVISION USING.description: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING allows you reference data being passed from a calling module to your program through the LINKAGE SECTION.

PROCEDURE IS.description: PROCEDURE DIVISION - The INPUT and OUTPUT PROCEDUREs are used to select specific records that will be released to a SORT - and process records returned from a SORT.

PROCEDURE-POINTER.description: A PROCEDURE-POINTER is a variable which contains the address of a procedure "entry point". PROCEDURE-POINTER variables are often used to CALL z/OS LE (Language Environment) utilities.

body: USE FOR DEBUGGING ON ALL PROCEDURES
USE FOR DEBUGGING ON ALL PROCEDURES.description: A USE FOR DEBUGGING keyword, which you can specify as ALL PROCEDURES once in a program.

PROCESSING.description: XML PARSE translates an XML document into individual pieces, then passes each piece to a user-written COBOL paragraph.

END PROGRAM.description: END PROGRAM designates the end of a called module and returns control to the calling module. The program name must be identical to its PROGRAM-ID.

PROGRAM-ID.description: IDENTIFICATION DIVISION - PROGRAM-ID provides a unique name for a COBOL program.

body: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING BY VALUE VAL AS ${2:BINARY-LONG}.

QUOTE.description: QUOTE/QUOTES is a figurative constant. It can also be used in a comparison or MOVE statement.

READ (QSAM).description: For QSAM file access, the READ statement makes the next record from a sequential file available to the program. In the given example, READ includes the INTO modifier, which moves the record from the I-O buffer into program WORKING-STORAGE, and the AT END modifier which forces z/OS to signal the program that the last record in the file has been read.

READ (VSAM).description: For VSAM (keyed) file access, the READ statement makes a specific record from an indexed file available to the program. In the above example, READ includes the INTO modifier, which moves the record from the I-O buffer into program WORKING-STORAGE, and the INVALID KEY modifier which forces z/OS to signal the program that no record was found in the VSAM file that matches the data in the key field.

RECORD.description: DATA DIVISION / FILE SECTION - As part of a COBOL FD, RECORD (singular) is used with the RECORD CONTAINS clause - which defines the size (in bytes) of each logical record in the file.

RECORDING.description: DATA DIVISION / FILE SECTION - As part of a COBOL FD, RECORDING MODE is used with QSAM files to describe the file/record data: F-Fixed (one record per/block), FB-Fixed/Blocked, V-Variable, U-Undefined (use for Load Modules) and S-Spanned records (extremely long records, that are larger than a block).

RECORDS.description: DATA DIVISION / FILE SECTION - As part of a COBOL FD, RECORDS (plural) is used with the LABEL RECORDS clause - which describes the I/O access mode (Sequential/Standard, Varying, etc.) for this file. This is typically used with QSAM files.

RECURSIVE.description: IDENTIFICATION DIVISION - An optional language element that allows programs to be reentered recursively.

REDEFINES.description: WORKING-STORAGE SECTION - REDEFINES allows one variable to share the same storage as another. It is a way to declare multiple fields for a single storage area in files and WORKING-STORAGE.

USING BY REFERENCE.description: BY REFERENCE receives an argument/address that was passed by reference (the default). You must define "COMMAREA" in the LINKAGE SECTION.

RELATIVE.description: Identify VSAM RRDS files in your program by using ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE. RELATIVE KEY IS associates a logical record with its relative record number.

RELEASE.description: RELEASE transfers records from an input/output area to the initial phase of a SORT. NOTE: RELEASE can only be used in an INPUT PROCEDURE SECTION.

RELEASE FROM.description: RELEASE FROM moves data from one group field to the SORT field, then transfers records from an input/output area to the initial phase of a SORT. RELEASE FROM can only be used in an INPUT PROCEDURE SECTION.

SERVICE RELOAD.description: SERVICE RELOAD, a compiler directive. It is syntax checked, but has no effect on the execution of the program.

REMAINDER.description: DIVIDE with REMAINDER allows you to specify a numeric data item that you can process as a remainder from the math. REMAINDER is available from all formats of the COBOL DIVIDE statement.

REMOVAL.description: FOR REMOVAL applies only to QSAM tape files.

RENAMES.description: RENAMES allows you to rename a data-item. The only level-number allowed for RENAMES is 66.

RENAMES THRU.description: RENAMES THRU allows you to rename multiple consecutively defined data items with the same name. The only level-number allowed for RENAMES is 66.

REPLACE.description: REPLACE allows you to rename a source text within a program file. This is typically used when the same physical record layout can assume multiple logical business terms within a program. This is a Compilation (not run-time) level statement that is similar to REPLACING except that it replaces text across an entire file - not simply a copybook.

REPLACING.description: REPLACING allows you to rename source text within a COBOL Copybook. This is typically used when the same physical record layout can assume multiple logical business terms within a program. This is a Compilation (not run-time) level statement.

RERUN.description: RERUN specifies what checkpoints (for rerunning a program) are to be taken at specified intervals.

RESERVE.description: RESERVE allows you to specify the number of I/O buffers to be allocated at run time for QSAM and VSAM files.

RESET TRACE.description: Deprecated but could still be syntax checked depending on your compiler release.

RETURN.description: The RETURN statement in the OUTPUT PROCEDURE of a COBOL SORT program is a request for the next sorted record.

RETURN-CODE.description: RETURN-CODE is a COBOL special register that can be used to pass a return code to the calling program or to z/OS when the program ends.

RETURNING.description: The RETURNING phrase specifies a data item that will contain the value returned from the invoked method.

REVERSED.description: REVERSED positions a QSAM file at its end. Successive READ statements make the file records available in reversed order, starting with the last record.

WITH NO REWIND.description: REWIND is typically used after WITH NO - an option that positions a QSAM file at its end.

REWRITE.description: REWRITE Can be used with any DASD (non-Tape) file. It replaces the contents of the current record with the program's FILE SECTION values for that record.

REWRITE FROM.description: REWRITE FROM can be used with any DASD (non-Tape) file. It moves data from (in the above example) WS-RECORD to the program's FILE SECTION declaration and replaces the record.

RIGHT.description: JUSTIFIED overrides COBOL's standard byte-movement rules for receiving data of type: PIC A, PIC X, DBCS, NATIONAL.

ROUNDED.description: After decimal point alignment, the number of places in the fraction result of an math statement is compared with the number of places provided for the fraction in the PIC clause. When the size of the fractional result is greater than fraction provided in the PIC clause, truncation occurs unless ROUNDED is specified. The right-most digit of the resultant is increased by 1 whenever the most significant digit of the excess is >= 5.

SEARCH ALL WHEN.description: SEARCH ALL item1 WHEN item2 EQUAL item3 item4

SUBTRACT.description: SUBTRACT A FROM B GIVING C
